newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian stocks strong, trend seen persisting.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian stocks strong, trend seen persisting.

text.p: Nigerian shares recorded respectable advances on Thursday, buoyed by rising volumes and a positive market perception which market operators said would continue.
The all-share index closed at 7336.57 from 7289.91 on Wednesday.
"We are in for a long bull run in this market. The odds are in favour of share trading now as all indicators point in the way of stability in the economy," one trader said.
Traders said the session was also characterised by generous gains by recovering stocks, although investors chose to sell the market's most capitalised company PZ industries to take profit.
PZ shares fell 10 kobo to 28.40 naira, down from 28.56 naira last Wednesday when its price was freed to move following the completion of a merger with Thermocool Engineering Company.
But demand for other leading stocks surged on the influx of cash into the market.

The big four banks rose, led by UBA which at 7.75 naira, gained 20 kobo. First Bank and Union Bank were up 15 kobo at 9.75 naira and 8.60 naira, respectively, while Afribank closed 10 kobo higher at 4.40 naira.
Food company Nestle went 50 kobo up again at 56.50 naira and Nigerian Bottling company added 40 kobo at 37.00 naira.
Union Dicon Salt rose 29 kobo to 45.60 naira following a successful annual general meeting on Wednesday.
Leading insurance firm AIICO shot up by 50 kobo to 13.25 naira as buyers scrambled for available shares.
Oil shares kept their eat. Agip topped the gainers with one naira rise to 26.00 naira. Unipetrol and Total were up 50 kobo each closing, respectively, at 68.20 naira and 65.00 naira.
Stocks recovering from recent slides were Lever Brothers, up 10 kobo at 17.10 naira and tyre maker Dunlop, which rose 40 kobo, its strongest one-day gain for many weeks to 8.60 naira.
Losers were few and included Benue Cement, which lost five kobo to 6.65 naira on big selling of its stock.
African Paints went down one kobo to 1.53 naira, the same margin as textile group Afprint which ended at 2.47 naira.
Nigerian Breweries and Guinness, leaders in their troubled sector were unchanged at 16.00 naira and 7.80 naira, respectively.
